text:
Tyler Toffoli has played for seven NHL teams and scored 309 goals before this season, and at 34 he is doing what he has always done: finding the net in San Jose. He has 6 goals and 13 points in 23 games, and nearly half of those points, 6, came on the power play. His expected goals, the quality of his chances, are 4.81, so the finishing is only slightly ahead of the process.

The thing to watch is his ice time. He is at about 13 minutes a night, and his last few games have dropped toward 10, with 9.4 against Nashville on Nov. 15. During that game, Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest noted Toffoli had played only 5:30 into the second period while his line kept taking shifts. A veteran on a team built around younger players, he may be getting his most important minutes on the power play rather than at even strength.

When he does play, the Sharks tilt the ice: at five-on-five they take about 51% of shot attempts with him out there and their share of chance quality is better than when he sits. Evolving-Hockey had him 110th among 401 forwards last season.
headline: Tyler Toffoli is still scoring as his minutes shrink
